published_prior_art.cite: AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT: standard transport-plan/flow representation and sparse LP architecture, but not the separate real/rational covariance-image statement.
HenrionNaldiSafeyElDin2021: exact algebraic SDP optimization under fixed dimension/variable regimes; it does not provide this prefix-Bellman certificate interface.

RaoZhang2025DDM gives a polynomial-time upper-only DDM guarantee; AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT treats fixed linear MOT costs. Neither states a fixed-row spectral, rational finite-support, locally checkable two-sided additive certificate.
Haus2015Mixability enumerates a fixed-row state space and AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT assumes a pricing oracle; neither gives certified spectral frontier pruning.
AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT Lemma 2.1 and HarmanEtAl2024OptimalDesignPolytope establish the relevant sparse-optimum and rational-support-reduction precedents.
The affine marginal-repair identity is a direct finite-mixture calculation; RaoZhang2025DDM establishes the target-marginal design setting but not this postprocessing formula.
No checked comparator exhibits this particular rational unequal-margin spectral instance with an irrational optimum and Bellman certificate.
Haus2015Mixability supplies the fixed-row pseudopolynomial and PARTITION boundary; this is a correct problem-specific specialization.

soundness_flags.label: ass:weighted-outcome-span
soundness_flags.one_line: The exact zero-residual restriction mu=B^T theta is a restrictive consumer model, not the standard Harshaw et al. condition cited under that name; retag it novel and justify its scientific setting, or cite a source imposing this exact span.

soundness_flags.label: ass:coefficient-ball
soundness_flags.one_line: The unit Euclidean coefficient ball is an additional normalization for the proposal's consumer risk, not a standard condition established by the cited Gram--Schmidt-walk result; retag it novel with an application-scale justification.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v2, 18 March 2025; nonprimary corroboration of theorem text
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3--4, Problem 3.1, Eq. (3), Theorem 4.2 and Eq. (6)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The text imposes prescribed assignment marginals, gives the HT MSE covariance identity, and states an upper guarantee f_B(D) <= (1+epsilon)^2 min{f_B(D_Bernoulli),1+1/epsilon}; it is not an additive instance-optimality guarantee.
Theorem 4.3 returns an optimal sparse MOT vertex using polynomially many ARGMIN calls, and Lemma 2.1 gives the standard sparse-MOT bound.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the exact outcome-span and coefficient-ball restrictions as novel consumer conditions, state the feature scaling and trial settings in which each is credible, and keep them explicitly outside the PrefixCert headline.

Sharpen Theorem 3 with a formal output-contract comparison table against Rao--Zhang: explicit law representation, exact rational marginals, lower witness, additive instance-optimal interval, checker complexity, and the fixed-row regime.
Add a worked nontrivial three- or four-unit lattice certificate, including the emitted path law and independently checkable Bellman inequalities, to make the claimed certificate interface concrete.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two mis-tagged consumer assumptions, retain PrefixCert as the field-level kernel, then advance the corrected core to Stage 0.
